result.topic_en: A simpler derivation showing that a displacement field (ξ, η, ζ) which leaves all infinitesimal distances unchanged must be a rigid motion, i.e. a translation plus an infinitesimal rotation with constant p, q, r.
result.transcription:
1836 Febr 18 \quad V p. 623 \quad Phys 9 \quad (1)
Viel einfacher wird die Ableitung auf folgende Art [-50-] 41
gemacht.
Wenn $x, y, z$ ; $x+dx, y+dy, z+dz$ die Coordinaten
zweier beliebiger einander unendlich naher Punkte sind
so muss die Variation von
$\partial x^2+\partial y^2+\partial z^2$
unabhängig von den Werthen von $\partial x, \partial y, \partial z$, $=0$ werden.
Zur Abkürzung bezeichnen wir
$\delta x, \delta y, \delta z$ mit $\lambda\xi, \lambda\eta, \lambda\zeta$, wo $\lambda$ ein
constanten unendlich kleinen Coefficienten bedeutet.
Man hat also
$\delta(\partial x^2+\partial y^2+\partial z^2) = 2\alpha(\partial x.\partial\xi+\partial y.\partial\eta+\partial z.\partial\zeta)$
$= 2\alpha\Big\{\frac{\partial\xi}{dx}.\partial x^2+\frac{\partial\eta}{\partial y}.\partial y^2+\frac{\partial\zeta}{dz}.dz^2$
$+\left(\frac{d\xi}{dy}+\frac{d\eta}{dx}\right)dxdy+\left(\frac{d\xi}{dz}+\frac{d\zeta}{dx}\right)dxdz$
$+\left(\frac{d\eta}{dz}+\frac{d\zeta}{dy}\right)dydz\Big\}$
Offenbar muss also sein
1) $0=\frac{\partial\xi}{\partial x}$
2) $0=\frac{\partial\eta}{\partial y}$
3) $0=\frac{\partial\zeta}{dz}$
4) $\frac{d\xi}{dy}=-\frac{\partial\eta}{\partial x}=r$
5) $-\frac{d\xi}{dz}=+\frac{\partial\zeta}{dx}=q$
6) $\frac{d\eta}{dz}=-\frac{d\zeta}{dy}=p$
2) $\frac{\partial p}{\partial y}=\frac{\partial\partial\eta}{\partial y.\partial z}=\frac{\partial\frac{\partial\eta}{\partial y}}{\partial z}=0$
Man hat aus (6) (4) oder (6) (5)
$\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial\partial\eta}{\partial x\partial z}=-\frac{dd\xi}{dy.\partial z}=-\frac{\partial r}{dz}$
[-$\frac{dq}{dy}=-\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}$ $\frac{dp}{\partial x}=-\frac{\partial\partial\zeta}{\partial x\partial y}=+\frac{dd\xi}{dydz}$-]
Also $\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}=0$ Ebenso wird
$\frac{\partial q}{dy}=0$, $\frac{dr}{dz}=0$
$\frac{\partial p}{\partial y}=0$, $\frac{\partial p}{\partial z}=0$ &c.
Also $p, q, r$ Constant
Also $\xi = a+ry-qz$
$\eta = b+pz-rx$
$\zeta = c+qx-py$

methods.what: Variation of the squared line element under an infinitesimal displacement field
methods.quote: $\delta(\partial x^2+\partial y^2+\partial z^2) = 2\alpha(\partial x.\partial\xi+\partial y.\partial\eta+\partial z.\partial\zeta)$

methods.what: Expansion of the variation as a quadratic form in dx, dy, dz (strain components)
Vanishing strain conditions (Killing equations): diagonal derivatives zero, mixed derivatives antisymmetric
Mixed second derivatives show rotation components p, q, r have zero derivatives
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial\partial\eta}{\partial x\partial z}=-\frac{dd\xi}{dy.\partial z}=-\frac{\partial r}{dz}$

methods.what: General infinitesimal rigid motion: translation plus rotation
